title: TODAY and NOW: the volatile clock

screens.prompt: In C2, work out how many days INV-1041 has been open, counting up to the day this drill pins as today (15 March 2024).

hints.syntax: TODAY takes no arguments, but it still needs the brackets: =TODAY()-B2.
hints.func-today: Ask Excel for the current date rather than typing one in: the column has to be right tomorrow as well.
hints.require-ref: Subtract the date in B2 so the next invoice is one copy away.
hints.no-now: NOW carries the time of day as well, which leaves a fraction of a day on the answer. TODAY is the whole number this column wants.
hints.value: 45366 minus 45352 is 14: check that you subtracted B2, the date raised, and not a neighbouring row.
hints.error: Dividing by zero comes back as #DIV/0! rather than a number of days: drop that part of the formula.

reject.why: today typed in as a number, so the column freezes at the day it was written
NOW is the moment rather than the day, and today's date is not in the formula at all
cancelling NOW back out still leaves the fraction of a day it carries
the date typed in, so changing B2 never reaches the answer
dividing by zero, so the cell holds #DIV/0! instead of a count of days
one day too many — 15 instead of the 14 days INV-1041 has been open
the closing bracket is missing and TODAY takes no arguments anyway

screens.prompt: In B3, return the hour the stamp in B2 was taken at, with the drill's clock pinned to 14:30.

hints.syntax: HOUR takes one date number and answers 0 to 23: =HOUR(B2).
hints.func-hour: HOUR reads the part of the number after the decimal point, which is where the time of day lives.
hints.require-ref: Read B2 rather than retyping the stamp.
hints.value: The stamp is 45366.604166667: the 45366 is the day and the .604 is the time. HOUR of it must land between 0 and 23.
hints.error: HOUR over text returns #VALUE!, and over a plain day number it answers 0.

reject.why: the minutes past the hour, not the hour
the stamp typed in, so a new reading never reaches the answer
TODAY is a whole day with no time on it, and the stamp in B2 is never read
dividing by zero, so the cell holds #DIV/0! rather than an hour
the next hour on, 15 instead of 14
the hour turned into minutes, so 840
the closing bracket is missing, so nothing runs

docs.explain: TODAY and NOW are the only functions in Excel that change without a cell changing. They read the clock of the machine the workbook is open on. A sheet recalculated tonight holds a different answer from this morning, and a copy emailed to another timezone can disagree with itself. TODAY answers with the day as a whole number, 45366 on 15 March 2024. NOW answers with the day plus everything since midnight, carried in the fraction after the decimal point, so 14:30 that day is 45366.604166667. Excel calls them volatile: they recalculate on every edit, even when nothing they read has moved. A workbook full of them is slower than one that writes the date into a cell once and points at it. The everyday pattern is a subtraction, where TODAY minus a raised date gives the days a job has been open. The trap is using NOW for it, which leaves a fraction of a day on an answer that should be whole. The second screen pulls that fraction apart. HOUR, MINUTE and SECOND read out of a date number the same way they read out of a typed time, because Excel stores both as one number.

errors.text: A date function was handed text that is not a date number: HOUR over a label, or a subtraction with a text date in it.
The date maths ran out of range, which happens when a subtraction crosses back before the first date this workbook can hold.
TODAY or NOW typed without the brackets, so Excel reads the word rather than running the function.

docs.atWork: An ageing report that says how many days each invoice has been open, refreshed by opening the file rather than by someone typing today's date into a cell. Plus a log row stamped with NOW, so the time of day survives alongside the date.
docs.outcome: Tell the difference between today's date and this moment, and read the time of day out of a date number.
docs.dataset: Invoices dated by day, and one log stamp timed to the minute

seo.title: TODAY and NOW in Excel: the clock functions
seo.description: TODAY gives the day as 45366, and NOW adds the fraction since midnight, so 14:30 reads 45366.604. Both recalculate on every edit, even with no change.
